Higher inequality reduces aggregate demand because the wealthy save a larger share of additional income, whereas lower‑income households tend to spend a higher proportion. This dampens consumption growth, the engine of many modern economies.

In short, trickle‑down economics rests on a false premise that wealth generated by the top tier will automatically and sufficiently benefit everyone.
